Front: What does mixed-precision training (AMP) do and what is the payoff?
Back: Runs most ops in 16-bit instead of 32-bit, cutting memory and speeding up training (especially on tensor-core GPUs) while holding accuracy. autocast picks precision per op; GradScaler keeps small gradients alive.

Front: What is autocast vs GradScaler in AMP?
Back: autocast chooses precision per operation (16-bit for matmuls/convs, 32-bit for loss/reductions). GradScaler multiplies the loss before backward so tiny fp16 gradients do not underflow to zero, then unscales before the optimizer step.

Front: What problem does gradient accumulation solve and how does it work?
Back: Simulates a larger effective batch when GPU memory cannot hold it (e.g. 128 x 2 = 256). Run forward+backward on each micro-batch (grads sum into .grad), call optimizer.step()/zero_grad() only every N micro-batches, and divide the loss by N so it matches a true averaged batch. Saves memory, not time.

Front: What does pin_memory=True do and when does it help?
Back: Allocates batches in page-locked (pinned) host memory so the GPU can DMA them asynchronously; pair with .to(device, non_blocking=True) to overlap copy with compute. Helps only when transfer-bound; otherwise it just wastes RAM.

Front: Name DataLoader knobs for keeping the GPU fed.
Back: num_workers (parallel loading subprocesses), pin_memory (async transfer), persistent_workers (avoid respawning), prefetch_factor (batches prefetched per worker). Goal: never let the GPU idle waiting on data.

requires_grad=False freezes weights (no updates). torch.no_grad() disables gradient tracking for inference (saves memory). model.eval() switches Dropout off and BatchNorm to running-stats mode. Three separate things.

Front: Shared two-step transfer-learning recipe (CV and NLP)?
Back: (1) Keep the pretrained backbone/encoder. (2) Attach a fresh task-specific head (new Linear for your classes / classification head on [CLS]). Then choose feature-extraction (freeze) vs fine-tuning (unfreeze, small LR) based on data size and domain distance.

Front: Augmentation: which split, and why exclude the others? (carry-forward mend)
Back: Apply to TRAIN only. Exclude val/test because evaluation must be deterministic to be reproducible and reflect real untransformed inputs. One line: augment train to generalize; keep val/test clean to measure honestly.
